prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
This 2005 manifesto sets out a programme focused on economic stability, public service improvement, security, opportunity, and international engagement.

Record and fiscal stance
- Claims: sustained growth, low inflation and interest rates, highest employment on record, rising incomes, reduced absolute poverty for children and pensioners, crime down 30%, faster asylum decisions, doubled aid, and early emissions trading.
- Commitments: maintain a 2% inflation target, borrow only to invest, keep net debt prudent; no rise in basic or top income tax rates; continue targeted tax credits; efficiency savings to redirect funds to front-line services.

Economy, jobs, business and infrastructure
- Goal of high employment via active welfare-to-work, higher minimum wage, reform of incapacity benefits with Pathways to Work, and stronger role for independent/voluntary providers.
- Support for enterprise: R&D tax credits, low corporation tax, science/innovation strategy to lift R&D to 2.5% of GDP by 2014; backing for manufacturing and fair public procurement under EU rules.
- Smarter regulation and competition policy; open energy markets; balanced energy mix including renewables, nuclear, clean coal, and microgeneration; promote green industries.
- Transport: sustained investment to 2015; rail reliability with possible high-speed routes and Crossrail; bus improvements and concessionary off-peak travel for over-60s/disabled; examine national road pricing; road safety measures; aviation in EU emissions trading; tonnage tax for shipping.

Education and skills
- Personalised learning; stronger teacher development and support staff; focus on literacy/numeracy with clear milestones.
- Every secondary to be an independent specialist school; expansion of Academies to at least 200 by 2010; Building Schools for the Future to renew facilities; tougher discipline powers.
- 14–19 reform: vocational diplomas designed with employers; more apprenticeships; EMAs; FE modernization and skills academies.
- Higher education: more places and science investment; variable fees capped at £3,000 with grants and bursaries; aim for 50% participation by 2010.

Health and social care
- Higher NHS investment, more staff, fewer waits; by 2008 a maximum 18 weeks from referral to treatment and free choice of hospital.
- More services in primary/community care; practice-based commissioning; new community hospitals; use of independent/voluntary capacity to add throughput at NHS standards.
- Stronger infection control; enhanced clinical governance; transparency on clinical trials.
- Public health: clearer food labelling; healthier school meals with new standards and inspection; restrict marketing to children of high fat/salt/sugar products; expanded smoking restrictions in enclosed public places and workplaces; more cessation support.

Crime, policing, migration and security
- Neighbourhood policing teams for every community; more Community Support Officers; single non-emergency number.
- Wider use of ASB powers; alcohol disorder measures; youth justice reform; expanded drug testing/treatment; creation of SOCA; tougher controls on guns/knives; stronger offender management and reoffending reduction; asset confiscation; better victim support.
- Migration: points-based system prioritising skills; English tests for settlement; civil penalties for employing illegal workers; faster decisions and streamlined appeals.
- Borders/identity: biometric visas, ePassports, electronic borders, and phased ID cards with biometrics.
- Counter-terrorism: updated offenses, control orders where necessary, international cooperation.

Families, older people, housing
- Child poverty: halve by 2010–11; support via tax credits, Child Trust Fund; universal early years.
- Childcare: Sure Start Children’s Centres nationwide; 15 hours free nursery for 3–4-year-olds; extended schools 8am–6pm; more childcare cost support; expanded parental leave (aim up to 12 months) and flexible working (consult on extending).
- Older people: Pension Credit uprated with earnings to 2007–08; rights to request work beyond 65; pilot individual care budgets; free off-peak bus travel.
- Housing: increase home ownership; higher stamp duty threshold; shared ownership/low-cost homeownership expansion; more and better social housing; nationwide choice-based lettings.

International, climate and development
- Active EU role; referendum on the Constitutional Treaty; euro entry only if tests met; NATO central to defence; maintain independent nuclear deterrent.
- UN, IMF, World Bank reform; arms trade treaty pursuit.
- Climate: 20% CO2 cut by 2010 (on 1990 baseline) and 60% by 2050; renewables, efficiency, emissions trading.
- Development: reach 0.7% ODA/GNI by 2013; push debt relief and fairer trade rules; support universal access to AIDS treatment and free basic health/education in poor countries.

Culture, media, digital and environment
- Increased arts/sport funding; free national museums; Creative Sparks in schools; wider sports participation, facilities, and competition; 2012 Olympic legacy.
- BBC governance via a new Trust; digital TV switchover 2008–2012; modernise IP law; film tax relief.
- Clean Neighbourhoods powers; higher recycling; protect green belt; brownfield-first housing; Code for Sustainable Buildings; Marine Act for spatial planning.

Democracy and devolution
- More neighbourhood and local council powers; support social enterprises; expanded youth volunteering.
- Council tax rises constrained; improve benefit take-up; review local finance.
- Further devolution in Wales, London, regions; restore Northern Ireland institutions contingent on end to paramilitarism.
- Lords reform: remove remaining hereditaries, codify conventions, time-limit bill stages; Single Equality Act and a Commission on Equality and Human Rights; strengthen anti-discrimination, including on religion-based hatred.
